name: Ghouls, Animal Ghouls and Revenant Families (Dark Ages)

pages.name: Ghouls, Animal Ghouls and Revenant Families (Dark Ages)

text.content:
The medieval world shuts down almost entirely at night, so a mortal ghoul with hands and eyes free to move by daylight is indispensable to a Dark Medieval Cainite. Ghouls are created and maintained just as in the modern nights, but a few specifics are worth spelling out for a 1230 chronicle.

Ghoul Abilities

  • A mortal becomes a ghoul upon ingesting one Trait of vitae. A normal mortal holds 10 Blood Traits; extremely old ghouls may store an additional Trait per century of age, but can spend only one Blood Trait per turn.
  • Ghouls do not age while Cainite blood remains in their bodies. Once past her natural lifespan, a ghoul who runs dry of vitae for even a short time ages to dust — days for most, but hours or minutes for very old ghouls.
  • Ghouls heal and boost Physical Traits with blood exactly as vampires do; without blood, they heal at the normal mortal rate.
  • A ghoul can regenerate a lost or injured limb by spending a Willpower Trait, spending Blood Traits (one for an eye or finger, two for a forearm or foot, three for a full limb), and winning a Physical Challenge. On a failed challenge, the ghoul makes two Simple Tests; failing either means the limb never regrows.
  • All ghouls gain the Prowess level of Potence within minutes of their first taste of vitae. Further Disciplines cost six Experience Traits per Basic level (with a mentor, usually the domitor), 12 for Intermediate (if the domitor is 10th generation or lower), and 18 for Advanced (if the domitor is 9th generation or lower).
  • Ghouls can frenzy like vampires but gain two Traits to resist, since the Beast's grip on them is weaker.
  • A ghoul who drinks five or more Traits of a vampire's blood temporarily gains that vampire's clan weakness until the vampire blood in her system drops back below five Traits.
  • A ghoul denied feeding from her domitor for a month develops a raging hunger: any time she can acquire vampire blood she must win a Self-Control Challenge to resist taking it, and after the first month without feeding she must also resist cravings for human flesh and blood (a Willpower Trait can subsume the craving for a scene; failing the Self-Control Challenge means she must satiate it immediately). A ghoul who goes long enough to fully purge vampire blood from her system loses all ghoul benefits and ceases to be a ghoul.
  • Ghouls are bound by the blood oath but cannot themselves grant it to others; most remain oathbound to their original domitor, an effect regular feeding reinforces even as neglect erodes it.

A vampire character who creates and keeps a ghoul must purchase the Retainers Background as soon as possible — one level per ghoul — and starts each session one Blood Trait down per ghoul kept (servants must be fed). Players should detail their ghouls' names, Abilities, Nature, and Demeanor, but the exact Traits a ghoul holds should stay with the Storyteller and should not exceed template norms without spending additional Retainers levels.

Animal Ghouls

Any beast can be ghouled and gains full ghoul benefits, remaining loyal only as long as it's fed. Ghouled dogs, wolves, and war-horses are the most common; a ghouled war-horse gains unnatural strength, speed, and tolerance for a Cainite rider. A domitor gains a Bonus Trait using Animalism on her own animal ghouls. Human-sized animals (like war-horses) hold up to 10 Blood Traits; smaller animals scale down — a dog holds six, a cat four, and a rat or bat two.

Revenant Families

Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} maintains several ghoul "families," the revenants, propagated by marriage and breeding across generations until the children are born with Cainite blood already in their veins and can generate their own vitae from around age 13 (regenerating one Blood Trait per day, so they rarely need to feed from a vampire directly; this blood does not slow aging but does power every other ghoul benefit). Only the offspring of two revenants have the greatest chance of being born a revenant. Each family carries its own inherited Disciplines and a weakness echoing a clan disadvantage.

  • @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.revenants.JournalEntry.IoQt3QoDDJZ8X4dz]{Bratovitch}: Foot-soldiers and huntsmen, the lowest-regarded family, coarse but unfailingly loyal. Disciplines: Animalism, Potence, Vicissitude. They frenzy as easily as the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah}.
  • @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.revenants.JournalEntry.wABwn8FJtAN2e88I]{Grimaldi}: Merchants, tinkers, and traders serving as the Tzimisce's eyes and ears in the mortal world; a comparatively recent and thinner-blooded family with only eight Blood Traits. Disciplines: Celerity, Dominate (ineffective on Cainites, but works on ghouls and mortals), Fortitude.
  • Krevcheski: Scholars and engineers who build siege engines and clockworks; distrusted for their fascination with the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} and rumored secret overtures to switch allegiance. Disciplines: Auspex, Dominate. Suffer a one-Trait penalty on Social Challenges at Tzimisce gatherings or wherever their reputation is known.
  • @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.revenants.JournalEntry.ldyqw2o2gR45LxDO]{Obertus}: The scholarly, clerical, and library-keeping wing of a Tzimisce monastic order, spread from Constantinople to Western Europe and the Fiends' homelands. Disciplines: Auspex, Obfuscate, Vicissitude. All suffer either @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.derangements.JournalEntry.9141ccd7ef544ebb]{Obsession}/@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.rules-reference-st.JournalEntry.7d3c86953d4f4dd6]{Compulsion} or @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.derangements.JournalEntry.77854e62fade40d8]{Perfectionism} (which may shift focus over time).
  • Santovich: Beautiful spies and infiltrators who marry into noble society to pull strings and report back, prone to sliding into hedonism and vice. Disciplines: Auspex, Presence, Vicissitude. Must win a Willpower Challenge or become addicted to any particularly pleasurable vice discovered.
  • Vlasy: Cavaliers descended from Magyar warriors, serving as horsemen, soldiers, and statesmen, said to have entered service to repay an old debt. Disciplines: Animalism, Potence, Presence. Every Vlasy must take the blood oath with a Tzimisce upon reaching adolescence.

Rumors persist of other, stranger Tzimisce-bred lines, and even whispers that the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} breed their own ghoul families.

vtmlarp.source: Faith and Fire (Dark Ages Vampire), Chapter Seven: Allies and Antagonists
